ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: Given that $AB$ is the diameter of $\odot O$, and $BD$ is a tangent to $\odot O$ at point $B$. Through point $C$ on $\odot O$, construct $CD\parallel AB$, intersecting $BD$ at point $D$. Connect $AC$ and $BC$. As shown in Figure (2), when $CD$ intersects $\odot O$ at point $E$, connect $BE$. If $\angle EBD=30^\circ$, what are the measures of $\angle BCD$ and $\angle DBC$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Given that,\\
$\because$ AB is the diameter of $\odot$O, and DB is the tangent of $\odot$O touching at B,\\
$\therefore$ DB$\perp$AB,\\
$\therefore$ $\angle$DBA$=90^\circ$,\\
$\angle$DEB$=\angle$EBA,\\
$\therefore$ $\angle$BDC$=90^\circ$,\\
$\because$ $\angle$EBD$=30^\circ$,\\
$\therefore$ $\angle$DEB$=60^\circ$,\\
$\therefore$ $\angle$EBA$=60^\circ$,\\
$\therefore$ $\angle$ACE$=120^\circ$,\\
$\because$ AB is the diameter of $\odot$O,\\
$\therefore$ $\angle$BCA$=90^\circ$,\\
$\therefore$ $\angle$BCD$=\boxed{30^\circ}$,\\
$\therefore$ $\angle$DBC$=\boxed{60^\circ}$.

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the right-side figure (2), A and B are the two endpoints of a vertical diameter on the circle, and O is on AB; draw a horizontal straight line BD to the right from point B, and BD is the tangent to the circle at point B; through point C on the circle, draw a vertical line parallel to AB, and this vertical line also intersects the circle at E and intersects BD downward at D, so C, E, D are collinear, and CD ∥ AB. Reasoning: It is known that ∠EBD = 30°. Because BD is the tangent to the circle at point B and BE is a chord, according to the tangent-chord theorem, the angle formed by tangent BD and chord BE is equal to the inscribed angle subtended by chord BE, so ∠BAE = 30°. Also because A and C are both on the circle, ∠BAE and ∠BCE both subtend the same chord BE, therefore ∠BCE = 30°. From the figure, C, E, D are collinear, and ray CE and CD are on the same straight line, so ∠BCD = ∠BCE = 30°. In addition, AB is the diameter passing through the point of tangency B, and BD is the tangent, so BD ⟂ AB; also CD ∥ AB, therefore BD ⟂ CD, hence ∠BDC = 90°. In triangle BCD, ∠DBC = 180° − 90° − 30° = 60°.
